scope.unit: bound (hadd) widths, all 12 signs x 5 planets, plus a tabular diagram

conditions.trigger: assigning the bound lord (sahib al-hadd) of a degree

conclusion.arabic: وأمّا الحدود ففي كلّ برج حدود لخمسة كواكب بدرج مختلفة فمن أوّل الحمل إلى ست درج منه حدّ المشتري ومن ست درج إلى اثني عشر درجة منه حدّ الزهرة ومن اثني عشر درجة إلى عشرين درجة منه حدّ عطارد ومن عشرين درجة منه إلى خمس وعشرين درجة حدّ المرّيخ ومن خمس وعشرين درجة إلى آخر الحمل حدّ زحل

scope.unit: face (wajh/decan) rulers, all 12 signs, plus algorithm

conditions.trigger: assigning the face lord (sahib al-wajh) of a degree

conclusion.arabic: فأما الوجوه فإنّه قسم كلّ برج بثلثة أقسام متساوية كلّ قسم عشر درج يسمّى كلّ قسم وجها وابتدأ من أوّل وجه من الحمل وهو من أوّله إلى عشر درج فجعل للمرّيخ ومن عشر درج إلى عشرين درجة للكوكب الذي يتلوه وهو الشمس ومن عشرين درجة إلى آخر البرج للكوكب الذي يتلوها وهو الزهرة
conclusion.engine_rendering: As for the faces: each sign is divided into three equal parts, each part ten degrees, each part called a face. He began with the first face of Aries, which runs from its start to the tenth degree, and assigned it to Mars; from the tenth to the twentieth degree to the planet following it, the Sun; from the twentieth degree to the end of the sign to the planet following that, Venus.
conclusion.worked_definition: each sign is divided into three equal 10-degree parts called faces (wujuh); Aries: 0-10 Mars, 10-20 Sun, 20-30 Venus, then Taurus's first face continues to the next planet (Mercury), and so on through the whole zodiac in one continuous Chaldean-order cycle
conclusion.algorithm: count complete signs from Aries to the sign before the target sign, multiply by 3, add 3, cast out sevens; count that many places from Saturn along the planetary (Chaldean) order to find the ruler of the target sign's first face; the next two planets in order rule the second and third faces
conclusion.cross_check: a full labelled table (jadwal al-wujuh) is also given for all 12 signs. This pass verified programmatically that applying the repo's own _face_ruler() function (src/engine/multitradition/hellenistic.py, Chaldean order with a +2 decan offset) at three sample degrees per sign reproduces exactly the three planets al-Qabisi's table lists for that sign, in all 12 signs with zero mismatches.

scope.unit: numerical essential-dignity scoring, 5 ranks

conditions.trigger: ranking the several rulership relations (huzuz) a planet holds at one place

conclusion.arabic: فإنّا نذكر قواها فيها وذلك أنّ صاحب البيت له خمس قوى وصاحب الشرف له أربع قوى وصاحب المثلّثة له ثلث قوى وصاحب الحدّ له قوتان وصاحب الوجه له قوة واحدة وبعضهم يقدّم الحدّ على المثلّثة
conclusion.engine_rendering: So we mention their powers therein: the lord of the domicile has five powers, the lord of the exaltation has four powers, the lord of the triplicity has three powers, the lord of the bound has two powers, and the lord of the face has one power. And some of them rank the bound ahead of the triplicity.
conclusion.named_alternative: al-Qabisi records that some (ba'duhum) rank the bound (hadd) ABOVE the triplicity (muthallatha) - i.e. a 2-rank/3-rank swap - without naming who; this is reported as a live fork in his own source tradition, not resolved.
conclusion.significance: this is a fully numerical point-scoring table for the five essential dignities, stated explicitly in 10th-century Arabic, roughly seven centuries before William Lilly's Christian Astrology (1647). The repo's own src/engine/multitradition/hellenistic.py currently documents the identical +5/+4/+3/+2/+1 scale as 'a later Latin development' and 'an anachronism' if applied to the Hellenistic section, attributing it to Lilly. Al-Qabisi's text shows the point-scale already fully formed in the Arabic tradition centuries earlier; Lilly's version is very likely a direct descendant of this Arabic (and its Latin translation lineage, e.g. John of Seville), not an independent Latin invention. This is reported here as a factual correction candidate for that comment; no code was changed as part of this pass.

exceptions: The bound-before-triplicity variant is recorded as 'some say' without an author name attached, unlike the Dorotheus citation elsewhere in this chapter.

scope.unit: explanatory analogy for the five essential dignities

conditions.trigger: explaining the qualitative sense of domicile/exaltation/bound/triplicity/face

conclusion.arabic: ومثل بعضهم ذلك فقال إنّ كون الكوكب في بيته كالرجل في منزله وضيعته وكونه في شرفه كالرجل في مملكته وسلطانه وشرفه وكونه في حدّه كالرجل في عشيرته وجنسه وكونه في مثلّثته كالرجل في حرسه وأنصاره وأعوانه وكونه في وجهه كالرجل في صناعته
conclusion.engine_rendering: And some of them likened this, saying: a planet's being in its domicile is like a man in his house and his estate; its being in its exaltation is like a man in his kingdom, his sultanate, and his eminence; its being in its bound is like a man among his clan and his kin; its being in its triplicity is like a man among his guard, his supporters, and his helpers; its being in its face is like a man in his craft.

analogy.exaltation: a man in his kingdom and sultanate (mamlaka wa-sultan)
analogy.bound: a man among his clan and kin (ashira wa-jins)
analogy.triplicity: a man among his guard and supporters (haras wa-ansar)

scope.unit: fully worked numeric example applying the 5/4/3/2/1 power table

conditions.trigger: determining the 'mustawli' (prevailing/overseeing planet) over a topic's place, using the point-scoring table

conclusion.arabic: فكان البيت الثاني الدالّ على المال خمس درج من الحمل والبيت للمرّيخ فله في الموضع خمس قوى والشرف للشمس فلها فيه أربع قوى والمثلّثة للشمس فلها فيه ثلث قوى فيكون فيه للشمس سبع قوى والحدّ للمشتري وله قوّتان والوجه للمرّيخ وله قوّة واحدة فيصير للمرّيخ ست قوى وللشمس سبع قوى فتكون الشمس المستولية على بيت المال
conclusion.engine_rendering: Suppose the second house, signifying wealth, falls at five degrees of Aries. The domicile is Mars's, so he has five powers there. The exaltation is the Sun's, so she has four powers there; the triplicity is also the Sun's, so she has three more powers there; so the Sun has seven powers there. The bound is Jupiter's, and he has two powers. The face is Mars's, and he has one power. So Mars comes to six powers and the Sun to seven powers; so the Sun is the one prevailing over the house of wealth.

conclusion.verification: arithmetic independently reproduced and confirmed correct during this pass: Mars 5+1=6, Sun 4+3=7, Jupiter 2; 7 is the maximum, so Sun wins, exactly as al-Qabisi states.

scope.unit: halb and hayyiz definitions

conditions.trigger: assessing whether a planet is in halb and/or in its hayyiz

conclusion.arabic: ومن حظوظ الكواكب العرضية الحلب وهو أن يكون الكوكب النهاري النهار فوق الأرض وبالليل تحت الأرض والكوكب الليلي بالليل فوق الأرض وبالنهار تحت الأرض فإن كان مع ذلك الكوكب الذكر في برج ذكر والكوكب الأنثى في برج أنثى قيل إنّه في حيّزه وقوّته كقوّة الرجل في موضع فوائده وكسبه وسعادته
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among the planets' accidental fortunes is halb: that the diurnal planet be above the earth by day and below the earth by night, and the nocturnal planet above the earth by night and below the earth by day. conditions.trigger: assessing whether the north Node (al-Ra's) and south Node/Tail (al-Dhanab) act as benefic or malefic

conclusion.arabic: وأمّا رأس الجوزهر فإنّه سعد وطبيعته مركّبة من طبيعة المشتري والزهرة ... وقال قوم طبيعته الزيادة فإن كان مع السعود زاد في سعادتها وإن كان مع النحوس زاد في نحوستها ... وأمّا الذنب فإنّه نحس وطبيعته مركّبة من طبيعة زحل والمرّيخ ... وقال قوم إن طبيعته النقصان ... فلذلك قيل إنّ الرأس سعد مع السعود ونحس مع النحوس والذنب نحس مع السعود وسعد مع النحوس
conclusion.engine_rendering: As for the head of the Dragon (the Node): it is fortunate, its nature composite of Jupiter's and Venus's nature [...]. And some say its nature is increase: if with fortunate planets it increases their fortune, if with unfortunate ones it increases their misfortune. As for the Tail: it is unfortunate, its nature composite of Saturn's and Mars's nature [...]. And some say its nature is decrease [...]. Hence it is said: the Node is fortunate with the fortunate and unfortunate with the unfortunate, and the Tail is unfortunate with the fortunate and fortunate with the unfortunate.
conclusion.primary_doctrine: the Node (al-Ra's) is benefic, its nature composite of Jupiter and Venus, signifying kingship, happiness, and wealth; the Tail (al-Dhanab) is malefic, its nature composite of Saturn and Mars, signifying lowliness, downfall, and poverty
conclusion.alternate_doctrine: some (qawm) hold instead that the Node's nature is simply 'increase' (amplifying whatever it accompanies, for good or ill) and the Tail's is 'decrease' - summarized as: the Node is fortunate with fortunate planets and unfortunate with unfortunate ones; the Tail is unfortunate with fortunate planets and fortunate with unfortunate ones
conclusion.firdaria_confirmed_elsewhere: both alternate views agree the Node's firdaria is 3 years and the Tail's is 2 years (see islam.qabisi.ch2.firdaria_full_duration_table)

exceptions: The two doctrines (fixed benefic/malefic vs. amplifier/diminisher) are both stated by al-Qabisi as live alternatives and are not merged into one rule here.

scope.unit: planetary rulership of the ages of life

conditions.trigger: assigning which planet governs a given age-span of the native's life, from birth

conclusion.arabic: وأمّا استيلاؤهنّ على العمر فإنّ القمر يبتدئ بالتدبير مع خروج الجنين فيدبّر مقدار سني الربية وهي أربع سنين ثمّ عطارد بعد ذلك عشر سنين ثمّ الزهرة بعد ذلك ثماني سنين ثمّ الشمس بعد ذلك تسع عشرة سنة ثمّ المرّيخ بعد ذلك خمس عشرة سنة ثمّ المشتري بعد ذلك اثنتا عشرة سنة ثمّ زحل بعد ذلك إلى آخر العمر
conclusion.engine_rendering: As for their rulership over the lifespan: the Moon begins governance from the child's emergence [birth], and governs the years of infancy, which are four years; then Mercury after that, ten years; then Venus after that, eight years; then the Sun after that, nineteen years; then Mars after that, fifteen years; then Jupiter after that, twelve years; then Saturn after that, to the end of life.
conclusion.cross_check: this is, year for year, Ptolemy's 'ages of man' chronocratory from Tetrabiblos IV.10 (Moon 4, Mercury 10, Venus 8, Sun 19, Mars 15, Jupiter 12, Saturn to the end). Al-Qabisi transmits it unchanged and without naming Ptolemy at this specific point (contrast islam.qabisi.ch1.exaltation_fall_table_and_ptolemy_disagreement, where Ptolemy IS named). This is a distinct system from firdaria: it runs once, in a fixed order, over an entire lifetime, rather than a repeating 75-year cycle.

exceptions: Al-Qabisi does not attribute this scheme to Ptolemy by name at this point in the text, unlike the exaltation passage; the Ptolemaic identification is this pass's cross-check, not the source's own claim.

scope.unit: planetary hour rulers and their gender

conclusion.arabic: وإذا كان يوم أو ليلة لكوكب من الكواكب فإنّ الساعة الأولى منه لذلك الكوكب والساعة الثانية للكوكب الذي يليه والثالثة للكوكب الذي يلي ذلك الكوكب مثاله أنّ يوم الجمعة للزهرة فالساعة الأولى منه للزهرة والساعة الثانية لعطارد والثالثة للقمر والرابعة لزحل
conclusion.engine_rendering: When a day or night belongs to one of the planets, its first hour belongs to that planet, its second hour to the planet following it, its third to the planet following that one. For example, Friday belongs to Venus, so its first hour belongs to Venus, its second to Mercury, its third to the Moon, its fourth to Saturn.
conclusion.rule: the first (unequal, 'zamaniyya') hour of any day or night belongs to that day's own planet; each following hour passes to the next planet in the descending Chaldean order (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon), cycling continuously
conclusion.gender: the first hour of every day and night is masculine, the second feminine, alternating for the rest of the day-and-night
conclusion.worked_example: Friday belongs to Venus, so its first hour is Venus's, the second Mercury's, the third the Moon's, the fourth Saturn's, and so on

scope.unit: sect, gender, and basic domain of each of the 7 planets

conditions.trigger: establishing a planet's fixed nature before layering condition on top of it

conclusion.arabic: زحل نحس ذكر نهاري ... وقال ما شاء الله يدلّ على اليهودية ولبس السواد ... المشتري سعد ذكر نهاري ... المرّيخ نحس ذكر ليلي ... الشمس سعد بالنظر نحس بالمقارنة وهي ذكر نهارية ... الزهرة سعد أنثى ليلية ... عطارد ممتزج ذكر نهاري يميل طبعه إلى ما مازجه من الكواكب والبروج ... القمر سعد أنثى ليلي
conclusion.engine_rendering: Saturn is malefic, masculine, diurnal [...]. And Masha'allah said: it signifies Judaism and the wearing of black. Jupiter is benefic, masculine, diurnal. Mars is malefic, masculine, nocturnal. The Sun is benefic by aspect, malefic by conjunction, and is masculine, diurnal. Venus is benefic, feminine, nocturnal. Mercury is of mixed nature, masculine, diurnal, its nature inclining to whatever planet or sign it mixes with. The Moon is benefic, feminine, nocturnal.

core_natures.Sun: benefic by aspect but malefic by conjunction (sa'd bi'l-nazar nahs bi'l-muqarana), masculine, diurnal
core_natures.Mercury: mixed/common (mumtazij), masculine, diurnal, inclines to whatever planet or sign it mixes with

conclusion.named_citations_in_this_chapter: each planet's description carries named-authority citations layered onto the base nature: Masha'allah is repeatedly cited for physiognomy and peoples/ethnicities associated with each planet (e.g. 'wa qala Masha'allah ... yadullu 'ala al-yahudiyya wa-lubs al-sawad', 'Masha'allah said [Saturn] signifies Judaism and wearing black'); Dorotheus is repeatedly cited for each planet's own lot and select temperament traits. These attributions are preserved by name rather than merged into a generic 'the tradition holds'.

exceptions: The Sun's split benefic-by-aspect/malefic-by-conjunction status is stated explicitly and is not the same claim as sect alone.

scope.unit: apparent light/size/speed variation by apsidal position; ecliptic-latitude classes

conditions.trigger: assessing whether a planet is strengthening or weakening by its own motion, independent of any other body

conclusion.arabic: فأمّا حالات الكواكب في أنفسها فهو أن يكون الكوكب صاعدا في فلك أوجه ناقصا في النور والعظم والسير ... وإذا كان بينه وبين أوجه تسعون درجة سواء فهو معتدل في النور والعظم والسير ... ومنها أن يكون الكوكب شماليا وهو إذا جاوز جوزهره بأقل من تسعين درجة فهو شمالي صاعد
conclusion.engine_rendering: As for the planets' states in themselves: a planet ascending in the sphere of its apogee is deficient in light, size, and motion [...]. When it is exactly ninety degrees from its apogee it is moderate in light, size, and motion [...]. Among these too: a planet is northern if it has passed its node by less than ninety degrees, and is then northern ascending.
conclusion.apogee_rule: a planet ascending in the sphere of its apogee decreases in light, size, and motion; less than 90 degrees before or after its apogee is still 'ascending'; at exactly 90 degrees it is 'moderate' (mu'tadil); beyond that it is descending in the apogee sphere and increasing in light, size, and motion
conclusion.latitude_rule: measured from the node in 90-degree quadrants: 0-90 degrees past the node is northern ascending; 90-180 is northern descending; 180-270 is southern descending; 270-360 is southern ascending

scope.unit: two named configurations distinct from ordinary aspect

conditions.trigger: checking for the Ptolemy-attributed 'facing' configuration, or for 'dusturiyya' (council/authority) status

conclusion.arabic: فمن ذلك ما ذكره بطلميوس من المواجهة وهو أن يكون بين الكوكب وبين الشمس وهو مغرّب ... ومن ذلك دستورية الكوكب وهو أن يكون الكوكب في حيّزه في وتد من أوتاد الطالع وأحد النيّرين في حيّزه مربّع له في وتد آخر بالنهار من الشمس وبالليل من القمر
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is what Ptolemy mentioned of 'facing' (muwajaha): that between the planet, occidental of the Sun, and the Sun [...]. Among these too is a planet's 'dusturiyya' (council/authority): that the planet be in its hayyiz, in one of the Ascendant's angles, and one of the two luminaries also be in its own hayyiz, square to it from another angle - by day from the Sun, by night from the Moon.
conclusion.muwajaha: attributed explicitly to Ptolemy: a planet is 'in the Sun's muwajaha (facing)' when, counting occidental from the Sun, it stands as many signs from the Sun's own domicile as its own domicile is from the Sun's (e.g. Saturn 6 signs, Jupiter 5, Mars 4, Venus 3, Mercury 2); analogously for the Moon, counted oriental of the Moon
conclusion.dusturiyya: a planet is in 'dusturiyya' (council/authority) when it is in its own hayyiz AND angular, while one of the luminaries is also in its own hayyiz and square to it from another angle (by day from the Sun, by night from the Moon) - a stricter, doubly-conditioned configuration beyond plain hayyiz

scope.unit: the combustion cascade, with a numeric cazimi-like threshold

conditions.trigger: classifying a planet's proximity to the Sun's rays

conclusion.arabic: وكلّ كوكب فمنذ يستتر بشعاع الشمس إلى أن يظهر من شعاعها يسمّى محترقا وأوّل ما يبدأ بالدخول في الشعاع يقال له بدأ بالاحتراق وإذا غاب في الشعاع وسار فيه يسمّى مغمورا وإذا كان مع جزء الشمس أو بينه وبينها ستّ عشرة دقيقة فما دونها وعرضه كذلك يسمّى صميما وإذا جاوز التصميم وهو يريد هناك أن يرى يسمّى مفلتا
conclusion.engine_rendering: Every planet, from when it is hidden by the Sun's ray until it emerges from that ray, is called combust. When it first begins entering the ray it is said to have begun combustion. When it is lost within the ray and moving through it, it is called submerged. When it is with the Sun's degree, or within sixteen minutes of it (or less), and its latitude likewise, it is called samim (the innermost state). When it has passed samim and is heading toward visibility, it is called escaping.
cascade: muhtariq (combust) - the whole span from entering the beams to re-emerging from them
bada'a bi'l-ihtiraq (begins combustion) - the moment of entering the beams
maghmur (submerged) - hidden within the beams while still moving through them
samim - within 16 arcminutes (or less) of the Sun's own degree in BOTH longitude and matching latitude condition
muflit (escaping) - past exact samim and moving toward visibility
conclusion.numeric_threshold: 16 arcminutes (0;16 degrees) defines samim, the tightest state of solar proximity - a cazimi-like threshold distinct from the general combustion (beams) orb.

exceptions: Al-Qabisi does not, in this passage, give the outer orb at which 'entering the beams' begins; only the 16-arcminute samim threshold is numeric here.

scope.unit: the synodic phase-strength cycle of Saturn, Jupiter, and Mars, with degree thresholds

conditions.trigger: classifying a superior planet's phase relative to the Sun through a full synodic cycle

conclusion.arabic: والثلثة الكواكب العلوية منذ تخرج من تحت الشعاع تسمّى شرقية ويقال إنّها زائدة في القوّة إلى ثلثين درجة من جزء الشمس وتسمّى بعد ذلك ثلثين درجة أخرى شرقية قويّة فإذا جاوزت الستّين يسمّى الكوكب شرقيا ذاهبا إلى الضعف
conclusion.engine_rendering: The three superior planets, from when they emerge from beneath the beams, are called oriental, and are said to be increasing in power up to thirty degrees from the Sun's degree; for the next thirty degrees after that they are called strong oriental; once past sixty degrees the planet is called oriental going toward weakness.
cycle: 0-30 degrees past emerging from the beams: oriental (sharqiyya)
beyond 60 degrees, until first station: oriental going toward weakness
first station to opposition: oriental retrograde
opposition to second station: occidental retrograde
second station to 60 degrees past the Sun (direct motion): strong occidental
beyond 60 degrees to 30 degrees before re-entering the beams: occidental going toward weakness
final 30 degrees: entering the beams again
conclusion.numeric_thresholds: 30 degrees and 60 degrees from the Sun are the two boundary points marking the transition into and out of the 'strong' oriental/occidental phases.

scope.unit: the synodic phase-strength cycle of Venus and Mercury

conditions.trigger: classifying an inferior planet's phase relative to the Sun through a full synodic cycle

conclusion.arabic: فأمّا السفلية فمنذ تفارق الشمس وهي راجعة تسمّى شرقية ضعيفة فلا تزال كذلك حتّى تنتهي إلى استقامتها فهي عند ذلك شرقية قويّة إلى أن يصير بعدها من الشمس كبعد الشمس منها عند الرجعة ثمّ تكون شرقية ضعيفة إلى أن تغمر في الشعاع
conclusion.engine_rendering: As for the inferior planets: from when they separate from the Sun while retrograde, they are called weak oriental, and remain so until they reach their direct station, at which point they are strong oriental, until their distance from the Sun equals what it was at the retrograde station; then they are weak oriental again until submerged in the beams.
conclusion.cycle: from separating from the Sun while retrograde: weak oriental; from stationing direct until as far from the Sun as at retrograde station: strong oriental; then weak oriental again until submerged in the beams, then samim, then combust moving toward emergence; symmetric occidental phases follow after heliacal rising in the west
conclusion.note: unlike the superior planets, the inferior planets' cycle is anchored to their own retrograde/direct stations rather than to fixed 30/60-degree elongation points.

conclusion.engine_rendering: As for their states with respect to one another: application, which is when the two planets are in beholding signs, and the swifter one's degree in its sign is less than the heavier one's degree in its sign, by six degrees or less; then it is said that the swifter one is heading toward application with the heavier one.
conclusion.ittisal_al_tul: longitudinal application: two planets in beholding (aspecting) signs, the swifter planet's degree in its own sign less than the slower planet's degree in its own sign by six degrees or less
conclusion.numeric_threshold: 6 degrees is the stated orb of application
conclusion.ittisal_al_ard: latitudinal application: additionally requires the two planets' ecliptic latitudes to satisfy their own matching condition (same-direction and same-trend for conjunction; mirrored trend for opposition)
conclusion.inqita: once the swifter planet's degree passes the slower one's, application is completed and separation (inqita') begins

scope.unit: khali al-sayr (void of course) and wahshi (feral)

conditions.trigger: a planet separates from one body without applying to another while still in its own sign; or a planet's sign is unaspected

conclusion.arabic: فإذا انصرف كوكب عن كوكب ولم يتّصل بكوكب ما دام في برجه قيل إنّه خالي السير وإذا كان كوكب في برج لا ينظر إلى برجه كوكب آخر ما دام فيه قيل إنّه وحشي
conclusion.engine_rendering: When a planet has separated from another and applies to no planet for as long as it remains in its sign, it is said to be void of course. When a planet is in a sign that no other planet beholds for as long as it remains there, it is said to be feral.
conclusion.khali_al_sayr: a planet that has separated from one planet and, while still in its own sign, applies to no other, is 'void of course' (khali al-sayr) - the general (any-planet) form of the concept usually reserved for the Moon alone in later Latin practice
conclusion.wahshi: a planet in a sign that no other planet beholds (aspects), for as long as it remains in that sign, is called 'feral' (wahshi)

exceptions: Al-Qabisi states khali al-sayr for any planet, not the Moon specifically; later authors' Moon-only 'void of course' is a narrowing of this broader concept, not a contradiction of it.

scope.unit: naql al-tabi'a (translation of nature) and radd al-nur (collection/reflection of light)

conditions.trigger: a swift planet links two slower planets that do not themselves connect, directly or through an intermediary aspecting body

conclusion.arabic: فإذا انصرف كوكب خفيف عن كوكب ثقيل واتّصل بكوكب آخر نقل طبيعة الكوكب الأوّل إلى الثاني ... فإذا لم يتّصل أحد الكوكبين بالآخر غير أنّهما يتّصلان جميعا بكوكب آخر فإذا نظر ذلك الكوكب إلى بعض مواضع الفلك ردّ نورهما إلى ذلك الموضع وهذا المعنى يقال له ردّ النور
conclusion.engine_rendering: When a light planet separates from a heavy one and connects with another planet, it carries the first planet's nature to the second [...]. When neither of two planets connects with the other, but both connect with a third planet, and that planet beholds some place in the sphere, it returns their light to that place - this is called the reflection of light.
conclusion.naql_al_tabia: if a light planet separates from a heavy one and connects with another, it carries the first planet's nature to the second; if it separates from a heavy planet and connects with one heavier still, the middle planet carries the lighter one's nature to the heaviest
conclusion.radd_al_nur_form_1: if two planets do not connect with each other but both connect with a third, and that third beholds some place in the sphere, it returns (radd) their light to that place
conclusion.radd_al_nur_form_2: if two planets do not connect with each other, but another planet moves between them (transfers between their degrees), it returns the light of one to the other - this too is called radd al-nur

exceptions: Al-Qabisi gives two distinct configurations under the single name radd al-nur; they are not the same mechanism and are recorded as two forms of one named concept.

scope.unit: man' (prevention/frustration), two forms

conditions.trigger: a third planet blocks an expected connection, by conjunction or by aspect

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك المنع وهو على وجهين أحدهما من مقارنة وهو أن يكون ثلثة كواكب في برج واحد مختلفة الدرج ويكون الثقيل أكثرها درجا والأوسط قد منع الأقلّ درجا من الاتّصال بالثقيل إلى أن يجوزه
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is prevention, which has two forms. One is by conjunction: three planets in one sign at differing degrees, the heaviest holding the greatest degree, and the middle one prevents the planet of least degree from connecting with the heaviest until it passes it.
conclusion.by_conjunction: three planets share one sign at different degrees; the heaviest holds the highest degree, and the middle planet's presence prevents the lightest from completing its application to the heaviest until it passes the middle one
conclusion.by_aspect: two planets share a sign, the lighter applying to the heavier by conjunction, while a third planet beholds the heavier by aspect; whichever of the conjoined and the beholding planet has the closer degree to the heavy planet 'wins' the connection, blocking the other

scope.unit: qabul (reception) and radd (return), with an angularity-dependent good/bad valence

conditions.trigger: a planet connects with the lord of a dignity it occupies, or with a combust/retrograde planet

conclusion.arabic: وإذا اتّصل كوكب بصاحب البرج الذي هو فيه أو صاحب شرفه أو غير ذلك من الحظوظ دفع طبيعة الكوكب إليه ... ومن ذلك الردّ وهو أن يتّصل الكوكب بكوكب محترق أو راجع فيردّ عليه القوّة لضعفه فإذا كان الكوكبان في وتد أو ما يلي وتدا كان ردّا بصلاح ... فأمّا إن كان الكوكب المتّصل ساقطا ... كان ردّه بفساد
conclusion.engine_rendering: When a planet connects with the lord of the sign it is in, or the lord of its exaltation, or another of its dignities, that lord gives its nature to it [...]. Among these is return: a planet connects with a combust or retrograde planet and returns power to it on account of its weakness; if the two planets are angular or succeedent this is a sound return; but if the connecting planet is cadent, the return is a corrupt one.
conclusion.qabul: if a planet connects with the lord of the sign, exaltation, or other dignity it occupies, that lord 'gives' its nature to the connecting planet (qabul, reception); if it holds a dignity itself and connects with a planet that also holds a dignity at that place, both natures are given
conclusion.radd: if a planet connects with a combust or retrograde (i.e. weakened) planet, it 'returns power' to it because of its weakness; if both planets are angular or succeedent this return is a GOOD return; if the connecting planet is cadent (while the other is angular/succeedent, or both are cadent), the return is a CORRUPT return

scope.unit: four named ways an expected application fails to complete

conditions.trigger: an application in progress is broken by retrogradation, interception, sign-change, or a third planet's own retrogradation

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك الانتكاث وهو أن يكون كوكب يريد الاتّصال بكوكب فقبل أن يتمّ اتّصاله به يرجع فيبطل الاتّصال ... ومن ذلك الاعتراض ... ومنه الفوت ... ومن ذلك قطع النور
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is intikath (breaking-off): a planet wishing to connect with another retrogrades before completing the connection, voiding it. Among these is i'tirad (obstruction) [...]. Among these is fawt (missing) [...]. Among these is qat' al-nur (cutting the light) [...].
conclusion.intikath: a planet heading toward connection retrogrades before completing it, voiding the application
conclusion.i_tirad: a lighter, faster planet than the one already applying retrogrades into conjunction with the target first, completing the connection ahead of the original applying planet and voiding its approach
conclusion.fawt: a planet heading toward connection changes sign before arriving, and a different planet already aspecting the new sign connects with the target instead
conclusion.qat_al_nur: a third planet, positioned in the second sign from the target, retrogrades into conjunction with the target and thereby 'cuts the light' before the original applying planet arrives; the same name covers the case where the target itself was about to connect with a heavier planet and that heavier planet's own retrogradation into a third planet cuts the transfer first

exceptions: These four are kept as four distinct named configurations, not collapsed into one generic 'frustration' rule, because al-Qabisi gives each a separate name and separate triggering mechanism.

scope.unit: lists of conditions making a planet fortunate, strong, unfortunate, or weak, with two numeric thresholds

conditions.trigger: a full accidental-condition assessment of a planet

conclusion.arabic: ومن منحسة الكواكب وفسادها أن تكون في مقارنة النحوس أو مقابلتها أو تربيعها أو تثليثها أو تسديسها أو يكون بينها وبين جسد النحس أو شعاعه أقلّ من حدّ كوكب ... أو يكون بينها وبين أحدهما اثنتا عشرة درجة فما دون ذلك ... فأمّا الشمس فأضرّ ما يكونان بها إذا كان بين أحدهما وبينها أربع درجات أمامها أو خلفها
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among the causes of a planet's misfortune and corruption: being in conjunction, opposition, square, or trine with malefics, or within less than a bound's width of a malefic's body or ray [...]; or being within twelve degrees of either node (or less) [...]. As for the Sun, the most harmful state with regard to it is being within four degrees of it, ahead or behind.
conclusion.fortunate_conditions: beheld by benefics via sextile/square/trine, or conjunct them; free of malefic aspect; besieged (hisar/ihtifaf) between two benefics or their rays fore and aft; oriental appropriately for sect; in bright degrees; received; in its halb or hayyiz; in a place of its own joy
conclusion.unfortunate_conditions: conjunct or aspecting a malefic; within an orb of a malefic LESS THAN THAT MALEFIC'S OWN BOUND-WIDTH at that point (a variable, bound-width-scaled orb, not a fixed number); in a malefic's bounds or domicile; a malefic overpowering it from the 10th or 11th place relative to it; within 12 degrees of either node (worse for the Moon); within 4 degrees of the Sun specifically (the tightest, most damaging proximity zone, distinct from full combustion); besieged between two malefics
conclusion.numeric_thresholds: 12 degrees (node proximity) and 4 degrees (Sun proximity) are the two explicit numeric danger zones in this passage.

exceptions: The malefic-orb rule is explicitly variable (scaled to that malefic's own bound-width at the point in question), not a single fixed degree value, unlike the 12-degree node and 4-degree Sun thresholds which are stated as flat numbers.

scope.unit: a full, asymmetric planet-to-planet friendship/enmity table

conditions.trigger: assessing whether two planets are naturally friendly or hostile to one another, independent of any specific chart

conclusion.arabic: فأمّا المصادقة فإنّ بعض القدماء قال إنّ المشتري مصادق لجميع الكواكب سوى المرّيخ وهي مصادقة له والزهرة مصادقة لجميع الكواكب وهي مصادقة لها إلّا زحل وزحل أصدقاؤه المشتري والشمس والقمر وأعداؤه المرّيخ والزهرة وهي له أشدّ عداوة
conclusion.engine_rendering: As for friendship: some of the ancients said that Jupiter is friend to all planets except Mars, though Mars is friendly to it; Venus is friend to all planets except Saturn, though Saturn is hostile to her, more fiercely than she to him; Saturn's friends are Jupiter, the Sun, and the Moon, and his enemies are Mars and Venus, she being the more hostile of the two.
conclusion.attribution: attributed to 'some of the ancients' (ba'd al-qudama'), not named individually

Jupiter.note: one-directional: Mars IS friendly to Jupiter even though this list does not name Jupiter among Mars's friends elsewhere in the same passage; the source's own list is asymmetric and is preserved as stated

conclusion.additional_enmity_types: two further named relations: planets whose domiciles are in opposition, and planets whose exaltations are in opposition, are each called a distinct kind of enmity ('adawa)
conclusion.strongest_friendship_rule: the strongest friendship is a shared nature in quality, temperament, and substance - e.g. Mars and the Sun agree in heat and dryness (and Mars is lord of the Sun's exaltation sign), Moon and Venus agree in cold and moisture (and Venus is lady of the Moon's exaltation sign)
conclusion.cross_tradition_note: a fully asymmetric natural friend/enemy table between planets closely parallels the 'naisargika maitri' (natural friendship) doctrine independently documented in the Jyotisha pack of this same corpus; this is recorded here purely as an observation for future cross-tradition comparison, not as a merge of doctrine, and no Jyotisha values are imported into this rule.

exceptions: The table as al-Qabisi states it is genuinely asymmetric (e.g. Saturn names Venus as an enemy 'more fiercely' than the reverse listing would suggest); this rule preserves the asymmetry rather than symmetrizing it.

scope.unit: the six recognized conjunction/ingress cycles

conditions.trigger: identifying which of six named periodic events is meant by 'the conjunction'

conclusion.arabic: فأوّل ذلك القران ... أعظمها اقتران زحل والمشتري في أوّل الحمل وذلك يكون في كل ّ تسعمائة وستّين سنة والثاني اقترانهما في أوّل كلّ مثلّثة وذلك في كلّ مائتين وأربعين سنة ... والثالث اقتران زحل والمرّيخ في أوّل السرطان وذلك في كلّ ثلثين سنة والرابع اقتران زحل والمشتري في برج برج وذلك في كلّ عشرين سنة والخامس نزول النيّر الأعظم نقطة الاعتدال الربيعي وذلك في كلّ سنة شمسية والسادس اقتران النيّرين أو تقابلهما وذلك في كلّ نصف شهر قمري
conclusion.engine_rendering: First, the conjunction [...]: the greatest is the conjunction of Saturn and Jupiter at the start of Aries, occurring every nine hundred sixty years; the second is their conjunction at the start of each triplicity, every two hundred forty years [...]; the third is the conjunction of Saturn and Mars at the start of Cancer, every thirty years; the fourth is Saturn and Jupiter sign by sign, every twenty years; the fifth is the great luminary's descent to the vernal-equinox point, every solar year; the sixth is the conjunction or opposition of the two luminaries, every half lunar month.
cycles: Saturn-Jupiter at the start of a new triplicity: every 240 years (12 conjunctions occur within one triplicity before the pair moves to the next)
Saturn-Jupiter sign to sign: every 20 years
the Sun's descent to the vernal equinox point: every solar year
conjunction or opposition of the two luminaries: every half lunar month
conclusion.conjunction_ascendant_definition: 'the Ascendant of the conjunction' (tali' al-qiran) means specifically the Ascendant at the moment the Sun enters the vernal equinox point in the year in which the (20-year) conjunction occurs

exceptions: This is mundane/cyclical doctrine, not natal; recorded for completeness of Chapter IV's definitions, refused as any customer-facing prediction.

scope.unit: the prenatal syzygy (namudar) and conjunctional/preventional classification

conditions.trigger: determining whether a nativity is 'conjunctional' or 'preventional' and locating the relevant prior-syzygy degree

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك النمودار وقد يظن ّ به كثير من المنجّمين أنّه يخرج به درجة طالع المولود بعينها وذلك خطأ وقد بيّنت ذلك في كتابي في النمودارات ... وقد قال بطلميوس إنّ جزء النيّر الذي فوق الأرض هو جزء الاستقبال وقد قال بعض العلماء إنّ تهيّأ للاستقبال أن يكون أحد النيّرين في جزء المشرق والآخر في جزء المغرب فجزء الاستقبال جزء المشرق وقال واليس إنّ جزء الاستقبال هو الجزء الذي فيه الامتلاء يعني جزء القمر
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is the namudar (pre-natal figure). Many astrologers wrongly think it yields the native's own Ascendant degree exactly; that is an error, which I have already shown in my book on namudars [...]. Ptolemy said the degree of prevention is that of whichever luminary is above the earth; some scholars said the degree of prevention is that of whichever luminary is in the eastern part; and Valens said the degree of prevention is the degree of fullness, meaning the Moon's degree.
conclusion.correction_of_misconception: al-Qabisi states explicitly that many astrologers wrongly think the namudar yields the native's own exact Ascendant degree; he says this is an error he has already demonstrated in his own book on namudars, and that it instead yields the first degree of the sphere properly belonging to the native after the Ascendant degree, in the natural direction of motion (though it often coincides with the Ascendant degree)
conclusion.classification: if the syzygy (new or full Moon) preceding birth nearest to birth is a conjunction (ijtima'), the nativity is 'conjunctional' (ijtima'i); if the nearer one is an opposition (istiqbal), the nativity is 'preventional' (istiqbali)
conclusion.named_dispute_on_the_prevention_degree: al-Qabisi records three named views on which of the two luminaries' degrees counts as 'the degree of prevention' at a full Moon: Ptolemy holds it is the luminary above the earth; some scholars hold it is whichever luminary is in the eastern (rising) part; Valens (Walis) holds it is the degree of fullness, i.e. the Moon's own degree
conclusion.tie_break: if more than one planet is equally dominant (most claims of dignity) over the conjunction/prevention degree, Ptolemy's rule makes the swiftest-changing one 'sahib al-hayyiz' (the hayyiz-holder) for this purpose

exceptions: The three named views on the prevention degree (Ptolemy, unnamed scholars, Valens) are preserved as three distinct attributed positions, not merged into one.

scope.unit: the full hyleg (prorogator) candidate-place algorithm

conditions.trigger: identifying which of five candidate points (Sun, Moon, prenatal syzygy degree, Lot of Fortune, Ascendant) may serve as the hyleg

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك الهيلاج في المواليد ومعرفته أن تنظر إلى وقت المولد فإن كان نهاريا تبدأ بالشمس فإن كانت قبل درجة الطالع بخمس درج فما دون ذلك أو كانت في العاشر أو في الحادي عشر مذكّرا كان البرج أو مؤنّثا فهي تصلح أن تكون هيلاجا ... وإنّما تصلح هذه الثلثة للهيلاجية إذا كانت في المواضع الثمانية التي هي الأوتاد وما يليها ... وكلّ موضع من المواضع التي ذكرناها إنّها تصلح للهيلاجية إذا ينظر إليها أحد أرباب الحظوظ الخمس
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is the hyleg in nativities. To know it: look to the time of birth. If diurnal, begin with the Sun: if it is within five degrees before the Ascendant degree (or less), or in the tenth or eleventh place - masculine or feminine sign alike - it is fit to be hyleg [... full candidate sequence for Moon, syzygy, Lot of Fortune, and Ascendant follows, with gender conditions on the luminaries and pure angularity for the other three ...]. And each of the places we have named is fit for hyleg-status only if one of the five lords of its dignities beholds it.
conclusion.day_birth_sequence: check the Sun first: eligible if within 5 degrees before the Ascendant degree (or less), or in the 10th or 11th place (any gender of sign); also eligible if in the 7th, 8th, or 9th place IF that sign is masculine (not eligible there if feminine); if the Sun is not eligible, check the Moon: eligible in the Ascendant, 2nd, 3rd, 7th, or 8th place (any gender); or within 5 degrees before the Ascendant, or in the 10th, 11th, 4th, or 5th place IF that sign is feminine (not eligible there if masculine)
conclusion.night_birth_sequence: the same candidate places, but beginning with the Moon, then the Sun, with the gender conditions applied symmetrically
conclusion.fallback_sequence: if neither luminary qualifies: check the prenatal syzygy degree (conjunction or prevention, whichever governs the nativity) for angularity; if not angular, check the Lot of Fortune's degree for angularity; if that too fails, the Ascendant degree itself becomes the hyleg by default
conclusion.angularity_requirement_detail: 'angular or near it' is defined precisely: a candidate degree counts as angular if it is within 5 whole degrees before the computed house cusp, measured by the equal-hour-based house division set out in the zij
conclusion.final_gate: even a place that reaches one of these eight positions is only hyleg-eligible if it is beheld (aspected) by at least one of the five dignity-lords of that degree (domicile, exaltation, bound, triplicity, or face lord); if none of the five lords aspects it, it fails as hyleg regardless of position

exceptions: The masculine/feminine sign condition applies ONLY to the luminaries' own candidate positions, never to the syzygy degree, the Lot of Fortune degree, or the Ascendant degree, which are evaluated by angularity alone.

scope.unit: the kadkhudah (alcocoden) selection algorithm, following on from the hyleg

conditions.trigger: having established the hyleg, selecting the planet that 'gives' the years of life (kadkhudah)

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك الكدخذاه وهو دليل كمّية العمر فإذا أردت معرفة ذلك وكنت قد عرفت الهيلاج بالطريق الذي قدّمنا ذكره نظرت إلى صاحب بيت الهيلاج أو شرفه أو حدّه أو مثلّثته أو وجهه فأيّهم كان أكثر مزاعمة في جزء الهيلاج وكان ينظر إلى الهيلاج كان أولى بالكدخذاهية ... وكان دروثيوس يقدّم صاحب الحدّ في ذلك على صاحب البيت
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is the kadkhudah, the indicator of the quantity of life. To know it, having already known the hyleg by the method given above, look to the lord of the hyleg's domicile, or its exaltation, its bound, its triplicity, or its face; whichever of these holds the greatest claim over the hyleg's degree and beholds the hyleg is the most entitled to be kadkhudah [...]. And Dorotheus used to place the lord of the bound ahead of the lord of the domicile in this.
conclusion.default_priority_order: domicile lord, then exaltation lord, then bound lord, then triplicity lord, then face lord of the hyleg's own degree - whichever of these, in that order, also aspects the hyleg's degree, becomes kadkhudah; if the domicile lord does not aspect, move to exaltation lord, and so on down the list
conclusion.named_disagreement: Dorotheus is cited by name as reversing this priority: he places the bound lord (sahib al-hadd) AHEAD of the domicile lord (sahib al-bayt) when both aspect the hyleg
conclusion.tie_break_rule_1: if two or three planets tie in dignity-claims over the hyleg's degree and all aspect it, the one with the strongest place (by angularity) wins; if place-strength also ties, the closer in degree to the hyleg's own degree wins
conclusion.tie_break_rule_2: an alternative named procedure ('some say') resolves ties by working strictly down the fixed order domicile-exaltation-bound-triplicity-face without regard to angularity or degree-closeness: whichever of these lords aspects the hyleg first in that fixed order is simply taken as kadkhudah
conclusion.tie_break_rule_3_solar_lunar: if several candidates still tie, the one nearest the Sun in the sense of the Sun's own favorable states (cazimi/samim, or heliacally rising, or in its first station) is preferred as kadkhudah
conclusion.collapse_case: if the hyleg itself is the Sun and the Sun is in Aries or Leo (its own domicile), the Sun is simultaneously hyleg AND kadkhudah, and no further search for a kadkhudah is made; symmetrically for the Moon as hyleg in Taurus or Cancer

exceptions: The default order (domicile first) and Dorotheus's named alternative (bound first) are both preserved; al-Qabisi does not adjudicate between them himself in this passage.

scope.unit: al-wali (the governor/overseer), a third significator after hyleg and kadkhudah

conditions.trigger: identifying the planet with the greatest overall claim across the nativity's key points

conclusion.arabic: فأمّا الوالي وهو المبتزّ على المولد ومنه يستدلّ على أحوال المولود بعد الهيلاج والكدخذاه فهو أكثر الكواكب مزاعمة في الطالع وموضع النيّرين وموضع سهم السعادة وموضع جزء الاجتماع أو الاستقبال الذي يكون قبل المولد ... وبعضهم يقيمه مقام الكدخذاه في عطيّة العمر
conclusion.engine_rendering: As for al-wali, the one that prevails over the nativity, from which the native's conditions are inferred after the hyleg and the kadkhudah: it is whichever planet holds the greatest claims over the Ascendant, the place of the two luminaries, the place of the Lot of Fortune, and the place of the conjunction or prevention degree preceding the birth [...]. Some place it in the position of the kadkhudah in the matter of the grant of years.
conclusion.definition: al-wali, also called al-mubtazz (the one that prevails), is whichever planet holds the greatest combined dignity-claims across the Ascendant, both luminaries' places, the Lot of Fortune's place, and the prenatal syzygy degree; if one planet overpowers two, three, or four of these places by weight of its dignity claims, it is al-wali
conclusion.function: al-wali is consulted, after the hyleg and kadkhudah, for the native's general conditions; some authors substitute it for the kadkhudah specifically in the matter of the grant of years

exceptions: Al-Qabisi records, without endorsing, that some authors use al-wali as a substitute kadkhudah for length of life; this pass does not adopt that substitution as a rule of its own.

scope.unit: burj al-intiha (the sign of arrival): whole-sign annual profection, with a full numeric worked example

conditions.trigger: given a whole number of completed solar years since birth, finding the profected sign of the Ascendant, Sun, Moon, Midheaven, and Lot of Fortune
conditions.method: count one sign per completed year, starting from the point's own natal sign, in zodiacal order; the sign reached after N completed years is the sign of arrival for year N+1; the domicile lord of the profected Ascendant sign is called 'al-salkhadhay' (a Persian loanword glossed by al-Qabisi as 'lord of the year')

conclusion.arabic: مثال ذلك أن مولودا ولد والطالع الجدي سبع عشرة درجة ووسط السماء العقرب ثماني درج والشمس في الحوت خمس عشرة درجة والقمر في الميزان خمس عشرة درجة وسهم السعادة في الأسد تسع عشرة درجة وكان قد مضى للمولود ثلث سنين تامّة فتنتهي له السنة الرابعة من الطالع إلى الحمل الرابع من الجدي سبع عشرة درجة وينتهي جزء القمر إلى الجدي خمس عشرة درجة ويكون المرّيخ السالخذاي وينتهي من موضع الشمس إلى الجوزاء خمس عشرة درجة والانتهاء من وسط السماء إلى الدلو ثماني درج والانتهاء من سهم السعادة إلى العقرب تسع عشرة درجة
conclusion.engine_rendering: An example: a native was born with the Ascendant at Capricorn seventeen degrees, the Midheaven at Scorpio eight degrees, the Sun in Pisces fifteen degrees, the Moon in Libra fifteen degrees, and the Lot of Fortune in Leo nineteen degrees; and three complete years had elapsed for the native. So the fourth year, from the Ascendant, arrives at Aries, the fourth sign from Capricorn, at seventeen degrees, and Mars is the salkhadhay. The Moon's point arrives at Capricorn, fifteen degrees. The Sun's place arrives at Gemini, fifteen degrees. The Midheaven arrives at Aquarius, eight degrees. The Lot of Fortune arrives at Scorpio, nineteen degrees.

worked_example_output.salkhadhay_year_4: Mars (domicile lord of the profected Ascendant sign, Aries)

conclusion.verification: independently recomputed during this pass using the standard formula profected_sign_index = (natal_sign_index + years_elapsed) mod 12: Capricorn(9)+3=Aries(0); Pisces(11)+3=Gemini(2); Libra(6)+3=Capricorn(9); Scorpio(7)+3=Aquarius(10); Leo(4)+3=Scorpio(7). All five outputs match al-Qabisi's own stated result exactly, and Mars is indeed Aries's domicile lord per the table in islam.qabisi.ch1.domicile_table_and_detriment.

scope.unit: world-year profection (burj al-intiha for the world), with al-Kindi's chronological data

conditions.trigger: profecting from the ascendant of a foundational conjunction to determine a 'sign of arrival' for the current world-year

conclusion.arabic: فأمّا الانتهاء من سني العالم فإنّ الكندي ذكر أنه كان بين سنة القران الدالّ على الملّة وبين الهجرة اثنتان وخمسون سنة شمسية وكان طالع سنة قران الملّة الجوزاء وانتهت السنة التي هاجر فيها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى السنبلة وبين الهجرة وبين يزدجرد ثلثة آلاف وستّمائة وأربعة وعشرون يوما
conclusion.engine_rendering: As for the arrival of the world-years: al-Kindi reported that between the year of the conjunction signifying the religion and the Hijra there were fifty-two solar years; the Ascendant of the year of the conjunction of the religion was Gemini; the year in which the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, emigrated arrived at Virgo; and between the Hijra and Yazdgird there are three thousand six hundred twenty-four days.
conclusion.al_kindi_data: al-Kindi reported 52 solar years between the year of the 'conjunction of the religion' (qiran al-milla) and the Hijra; the Ascendant of the conjunction-of-religion year was Gemini; the year in which the Prophet emigrated (the Hijra) arrived at Virgo; between the Hijra and the Yazdgird era lie 3624 days
conclusion.alternate_method: a different, unnamed authority ('other than al-Kindi') instead adds 61 years, 2 months, 12 days, and 16 Persian hours to the completed Yazdgird years, and profects from Libra (for the conjunction-of-religion arrival), from Scorpio (for the arrival of the conjunction itself), or from Virgo minus specific year-offsets (117 years for the 'ascendant of the dynasty', 176 years for the watery-to-fiery triplicity transition)

exceptions: This is explicitly mundane/dynastic chronology; two different named computational traditions (al-Kindi vs. an unnamed alternative) are preserved separately, not merged.

scope.unit: tasyir (direction/progression by right and oblique ascension), with a numeric rate

conditions.trigger: directing a significator to a promittor by ascensional arc

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك التسيير وهو أن تسيّر دليلا ما إلى موضع ما من فلك البروج فتعرف ما بينهما من درج معدّل النهار ... فيؤخذ لكلّ درجة سنة ... وبعضهم يرى أن تسيير أدلّاء السنة لكلّ تسع وخمسين دقيقة وثماني ثواني يوم ... والأدلّاء التي تسير هي درجة الطالع وجزء الشمس وجزء القمر وجزء سهم السعادة وجزء وسط السماء
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is tasyir (direction): that you direct some significator to some place in the zodiac, and find the arc of right ascension between them [...]; a year is taken for each degree [...]. And some hold that the significators of the (annual) revolution are directed at a rate of fifty-nine minutes eight seconds per day. [...] And the significators that are directed are the Ascendant's degree, the Sun's point, the Moon's point, the Lot of Fortune's point, and the Midheaven's point.
conclusion.method_summary: convert the arc between the significator's degree and the target degree into ascensional time using right ascensions (for angular significators) or a proportional 'hours from the angle' equation (for succeedent/cadent significators), then convert that arc into years at a fixed rate
conclusion.rate: one degree of ascensional arc equals one year
conclusion.world_year_rate: for revolutions of the year (of the world or of a nativity), directions of the significators run at 59 minutes 8 seconds of arc per day instead of the general degree-per-year rate
conclusion.numeric_cross_check: 59 arcminutes 8 arcseconds equals 59.1333 arcminutes, i.e. approximately 0.98556 degrees per day; this is within about a third of an arcsecond of the modern mean solar motion of 360/365.2422 = 0.985647 degrees/day (59 arcminutes 8.3 arcseconds). Al-Qabisi's stated constant is therefore the mean solar motion, given directly, roughly four centuries before this same constant is often cited in Latin sources under the name 'Naibod' (a much later medieval attribution).
conclusion.significators_that_are_directed: the Ascendant degree, the Sun's degree, the Moon's degree, the Lot of Fortune's degree, and the Midheaven degree, each governing a distinct topical domain (Ascendant: bodily accidents; Sun: fortune/eminence/rule; Moon: the soul and its states; Lot of Fortune: earnings and hardship; Midheaven: profession and governance)

exceptions: The degree-per-year rate and the 59'8'-per-day rate are two different constants for two different purposes (general directions vs. year-revolution directions specifically) and are not interchangeable.

scope.unit: al-jarbakhtar: a distinct time-lord system directing through the bounds

conditions.trigger: an alternative directional/time-lord technique keyed to the Ascendant's own bound (hadd) sequence

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك الجار بختار في المواليد وهو تسيير درجة الطالع وذلك أن تنظر إلى الطالع في حدّ أيّ كوكب هو وتنقص مطالع الطالع في البلد من مطالع آخر حدّ ذلك الكوكب فما بقي أخذت لكلّ درجة سنة ولكلّ خمس دقائق شهرا ولكلّ دقيقة ستّة أيّام وكان صاحب الحدّ يدبر تلك السنين وهو القاسم
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is al-jarbakhtar in nativities, which is the direction of the Ascendant's degree: look to which planet's bound the Ascendant is in, and subtract the Ascendant's oblique ascension for the locality from the oblique ascension of that bound's ending point; what remains, take a year for each degree, a month for every five minutes, and six days for every minute; and the lord of that bound governs those years, and he is 'the divider' (al-qasim).
conclusion.method: find which planet's bound holds the Ascendant degree; measure the ascensional arc (by oblique ascension for the locality) from the Ascendant to the end of that bound; the bound's lord governs that many years of life, at the stated conversion rate; when that bound's years are exhausted, the lord of the NEXT bound in the sign (and, at the sign's end, the next sign's first bound) takes over, continuing this way for the rest of life
conclusion.conversion_rate: 1 degree = 1 year; 5 arcminutes = 1 month; 1 arcminute = 6 days
conclusion.internal_consistency_check: the three rates are mutually consistent under a schematic 360-day year of 12 thirty-day months: 5' x 12 months = 60' = 1 degree = 1 year; and 1' x 6 days x 5 = 30 days = 1 month. All three conversions describe the same underlying 360-day schematic calendar.

scope.unit: al-ithna 'ashariyya (duodecatemoria), for planets or house cusps

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك الاثنا عشرية للكواكب والبيوت وهو أن تنظر ما سار الكوكب في برجه أو درج البيت الذي تريد من الدرج والدقائق فتضرب ذلك في اثني عشر ثمّ تعد ّ من أوّل البرج الذي تلك الدرج منه لكلّ برج ثلثين درجة فحيث نفد العدد فثم ّ اثنا عشرية الكوكب أو البيت
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is the duodecatemorion for planets and house-cusps: look at how far the planet has traveled in its sign, or the cusp's degree and minutes; multiply that by twelve; then count from the start of the sign that figure belongs to, allotting thirty degrees per sign; wherever the count ends is the duodecatemorion of the planet or the cusp.
conclusion.formula: take the degrees and minutes the planet (or cusp) has traveled within its own sign, multiply by 12, then count that many degrees from the start of the sign the resulting figure falls in, allotting 30 degrees per sign as you count; wherever the count ends is the duodecatemorion

scope.unit: al-nawbahrat (the ninth-parts), with a worked mini-example

conditions.trigger: dividing a sign into nine equal parts and assigning each a ruler by triplicity sequence

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك النوبهرات وهي الأتساع ... مثال ذلك أن البرج الذي كانت تلك الدرجة منه في مثلّثة الحمل ... وإن كان كوكب أو بيت من البيوت في ثماني عشرة درجة من الدلو فإذا قسم البرج بتسعة أقسام كانت الدرجة الثامنة عشر في القسم السادس ... فيكون صاحب نوبهرة الدرجة الثامنة عشر المشتري
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is al-nawbahrat, the ninths [...]. For example: if a planet or house-cusp is at eighteen degrees of Aquarius, dividing the sign into nine parts places the eighteenth degree in the sixth part [...], so the lord of the ninth-part of the eighteenth degree is Jupiter.
conclusion.method: divide the sign into nine equal parts of 3 degrees 20 minutes each; the first ninth is ruled by the lord of the sign's own triplicity in that sign; the following ninths are ruled by the lords of each subsequent sign in zodiacal order, continuing the triplicity-based cycle
conclusion.worked_example: 18 degrees of Aquarius: dividing the sign into nine parts of 3;20 each places 18 degrees in the sixth part (16;40-20;00); Aquarius belongs to the airy triplicity (Libra's triplicity in this text's convention), so counting Venus(Libra)/Mars(Scorpio)/Jupiter(Sagittarius)/Saturn(Capricorn)/Saturn(Aquarius)/Jupiter(Pisces) through six ninths lands on Jupiter; al-Qabisi states the answer directly: the lord of the ninth-part of the eighteenth degree (of Aquarius) is Jupiter.
conclusion.cross_tradition_note: this ninth-fold subdivision, ruled cyclically by the same-triplicity domicile lords, is structurally the same construction as the 'navamsha' (ninth-harmonic) division independently documented in the Jyotisha pack of this corpus. This is recorded purely as an observation of a shared Perso-Indo-Arabic technical inheritance; no Jyotisha rule or value is imported, and no claim is made here about which tradition originated it.

scope.unit: al-darijan: a triplicity-based threefold division specific to the Ascendant

conditions.trigger: dividing the Ascendant sign itself (not a general planetary degree) into three 10-degree parts

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك الدريجان وهو أن تقسم الطالع بثلثة أقسام كلّ قسم عشر درج فتجعل القسم الأوّل لربّ الطالع والقسم الثاني لربّ الخامس والقسم الثالث لربّ التاسع والطالع والخامس والتاسع أبدا مثلّثة مثاله أن الطالع الحمل ما بين أوّله إلى عشر درج فيكون دريجانه المرّيخ
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is al-darijan: you divide the Ascendant into three parts, each ten degrees, and assign the first part to the lord of the Ascendant, the second part to the lord of the fifth, and the third to the lord of the ninth - the Ascendant, fifth, and ninth always being one triplicity. For example: if the Ascendant is Aries, from its start to ten degrees, its darijan is Mars.
conclusion.method: the Ascendant sign's first 10 degrees are ruled by the lord of the Ascendant sign; the second 10 degrees by the lord of the 5th sign from the Ascendant; the third 10 degrees by the lord of the 9th - since the Ascendant, 5th, and 9th are always one triplicity
conclusion.worked_example: for Ascendant Aries: 0-10 degrees ruled by Mars (lord of Aries), 10-20 by the Sun (lord of Leo, the 5th), 20-30 by Jupiter (lord of Sagittarius, the 9th)
conclusion.distinctness_note: this is a DIFFERENT threefold division from the ordinary Chaldean face/decan table (islam.qabisi.ch1.face_table_chaldean_order): darijan applies only to the Ascendant sign and uses the Ascendant-5th-9th triplicity lords, not the continuous Chaldean cycle.

scope.unit: sahib al-dawr: an hour-lord-to-house/year rotation system, distinct from firdaria and profection

conditions.trigger: assigning yearly rulers by the sequence of planetary hour-lords counted from the hour of birth

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك صاحب الدور في المواليد وهو أن تنظر إلى ربّ الساعة التي ولد فيها المولود فتجعل للطالع وللسنة الأولى من ولادته ... وتجعل ربّ الساعة الثانية منه للبيت الثاني من الطالع وللسنة الثانية ... ومنهم من يجعل صاحب الدور صاحب طالع الأصل لأوّل سنة والسنة الثانية للكوكب الذي يليه
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is sahib al-dawr (lord of the rotation) in nativities: look to the lord of the hour in which the native was born, and assign it to the Ascendant and to the first year of life [...]; assign the lord of the second hour after it to the second house from the Ascendant and to the second year [...]. And some of them make sahib al-dawr instead the lord of the radical Ascendant for the first year, and the planet following it for the second year.
conclusion.method: the lord of the hour in which the native was born governs the Ascendant and the first year of life; the lord of the second hour after birth governs the 2nd house and the 2nd year; the lord of the third hour governs the 3rd house and 3rd year; and so on in strict parallel, each successive birth-hour's lord mapped to the correspondingly numbered house AND the correspondingly numbered year (continuing past the 12th house/year by wrapping back to the 1st house with the 13th hour-lord, etc.)
conclusion.naming_convention: each hour-lord in this sequence is named after its assigned house (e.g. 'lord of the Ascendant-hour', 'lord of the wealth-house-hour') and, collectively, the whole sequence is also called 'sahib al-dawr' (lord of the cycle/rotation); it is consulted for that year's affairs the same way the corresponding house's own ordinary lord would be consulted, and cross-referenced the same way as the annual profection's salkhadhay
conclusion.named_alternative: some (minhum) instead assign the natal Ascendant-lord itself to the first year, the next planet in sequence to the second year, and so on - paralleling the hour-lord method but starting from the Ascendant's own domicile lord rather than the birth-hour sequence

exceptions: This is presented as a fourth distinct time-lord technique in this same chapter, alongside firdaria, annual (whole-sign) profection, and primary/bound-directions; it is not treated as identical to any of them.

scope.unit: al-mamarr: one planet 'passing over' another, with a numeric conversion constant

conditions.trigger: determining which of two conjoining/aspecting planets is said to 'pass over' the other

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك الممرّ فإنّه يقال إن الكوكب يمر ّ فوق الكوكب ... ثمّ تنقص بعد الوقوف على ذلك أقلّهما من أكثرهما وتضرب ما يبقى في سبعة وتقسم على اثنين وعشرين فما خرج من القسم كان ذلك لكلّ كوكب مقدار صعوده أو هبوطه
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is passage (mamarr): it is said that one planet passes over another [...]. Having established this, subtract the lesser of the two [ascent/descent amounts] from the greater, multiply the remainder by seven, and divide by twenty-two; the quotient is, for each planet, its amount of ascent or descent.
conclusion.rule: compare each planet's mean position to its equated (true) position: a planet whose true position is less than its mean is ascending from mid-orbit toward its apogee; if more, it is descending toward perigee; take the difference between the two planets' amounts of ascent/descent, multiply by 7, divide by 22, and the result is each planet's degree of passage
conclusion.numeric_constant: 7/22 (approximately 0.318) is the stated multiplier/divisor pair used to convert the raw positional difference into the passage amount
conclusion.directional_rule: an ascending planet passes over a descending one; between two ascending or two descending planets, the one with greater northern latitude (or lesser southern latitude) passes over the other; conjunction-based passage is said to show the strongest effect, square and opposition-based comparisons weaker
conclusion.venus_mercury_variant: for Venus and Mercury specifically, when oriental, the comparison is instead made against the Sun's own equated position rather than the planet's own mean/true difference

scope.unit: al-bust: an India-attributed post-conjunction hour system, with a war-omen doctrine

conditions.trigger: assigning planetary rulers to sequential 12-hour blocks after a Sun-Moon conjunction for electional timing

conclusion.arabic: ومن ذلك البست وهو شيء كانت تعمل به الهند كثيرا ... وقال قوم البست هو أن تعد ّ بعد الاجتماع اثنتا عشرة ساعة زمانية تسمّى محترقة لا ينبغي لأحد أن يبتدئ فيها بعمل ... فقالوا من ابتدأ في الأربع ساعات الأولى بالحرب خيف على نفسه التلف
conclusion.engine_rendering: Among these is al-bust, a thing the people of India used to practice a great deal [...]. And some said al-bust is that you count, after the conjunction, twelve temporal hours called combust, in which no one should begin any undertaking [...]. They said: whoever begins war in the first four hours risks death to himself.
conclusion.attribution: explicitly attributed to India: 'a thing the people of India used to practice a great deal' (shay' kanat ta'malu bihi al-Hind kathiran)
conclusion.method_1: count 12 hours after the conjunction, assign them to the Sun, subdivided into three 4-hour blocks each ruled by the Sun's own triplicity lords at the conjunction moment; the next 12 hours go to Venus (again split into thirds by Venus's triplicity lords), then Mercury, and so on through the planets in order, the full cycle returning to the Sun after 84 hours (12x7), repeating continuously until the next conjunction
conclusion.method_2_alternate: a different group holds instead that the 12 hours immediately after conjunction are 'combust' (muhtariqa) hours in which no one should begin any undertaking; the following 72 hours are 'not combust' and suitable for beginning actions; then 12 more combust hours, cycling to the next conjunction
conclusion.war_omen_subdivision: the alternate view further subdivides the 12 combust hours into three 4-hour blocks with specific war-timing omens: beginning a war in the first 4 hours risks death to the actor himself; in the second 4 hours, risk of bodily calamity without death; in the last 4 hours, risk of great calamity to one's wealth, property, associates, and dependents

exceptions: Al-Qabisi presents this material himself as marginal (see islam.qabisi.ch5.commodity_price_lots_self_declared_weak for his parallel disclaimer about the adjoining weak-doctrine lots); it is recorded for completeness of Chapter IV, not as endorsed doctrine.

scope.unit: the general lot-casting method, worked for the Lot of Fortune

conditions.trigger: casting any lot described by the chapter's standard 'take from X to Y, cast from the Ascendant' phrasing

conclusion.arabic: وإذا قلنا في بعض السهام خذ من موضع كذا إلى موضع كذا وألقه من الطالع أو من موضع آخر وهو أن تزيد على ما بين الموضعين درج الطالع أو الدرج التي في ذلك البرج الذي تلقي منه ثمّ تلقي ذلك من أوّل برج الطالع أو من أوّل البرج الذي يلقى منه مثال ذلك عمل سهم السعادة فإنّك تأخذ ما بين الشمس والقمر وتلقيه من الطالع
conclusion.engine_rendering: When we say, of some lot, 'take from such a place to such a place, and cast it from the Ascendant,' this means: add to the arc between the two places the Ascendant's own degree, or the degree within the sign you are casting from, then cast that total from the start of the Ascendant's sign, or the start of the sign you are casting from. For example, the working of the Lot of Fortune: you take the arc between the Sun and the Moon and cast it from the Ascendant.
conclusion.general_method: when a lot is described as 'take from place A to place B, and cast it from the Ascendant (or another named place)', this means: add the Ascendant's own degree-distance to the arc from A to B, then count that total forward from the start of the sign you are casting from
conclusion.lot_of_fortune_worked: take the arc from the Sun to the Moon, and cast it from the Ascendant, i.e. add the Ascendant's degree to that arc and count forward from the start of the Ascendant's sign; wherever the count ends is the Lot of Fortune's place
conclusion.day_night_reversal: implicit throughout the chapter via the 'by day ... by night the reverse' formula attached to nearly every individual lot below

scope.unit: two rare, directly-hyleg-linked lots: the Lot of Life and the Lot of the Hyleg

conditions.trigger: casting these two 1st-house lots

conclusion.arabic: سهم الحياة يؤخذ بالنهار من المشتري إلى زحل وبالليل مخالفا ويلقى من الطالع سهم الهيلاج يؤخذ من جزء الاجتماع أو الاستقبال الذي يكون قبل المولد إلى درجة القمر ويلقى من الطالع
conclusion.engine_rendering: The Lot of Life: taken by day from Jupiter to Saturn, by night the reverse, cast from the Ascendant. The Lot of the Hyleg: taken from the degree of the conjunction or prevention preceding the birth to the Moon's degree, cast from the Ascendant.
conclusion.lot_of_life: by day, from Jupiter to Saturn; by night, the reverse; cast from the Ascendant
conclusion.lot_of_hyleg: from the prenatal conjunction-or-prevention degree (whichever governs the nativity) to the Moon's degree, cast from the Ascendant - notably NOT reversed by sect the way most other lots in this chapter are
conclusion.significance: a Lot explicitly named for and tied to the hyleg concept (islam.qabisi.ch4.hyleg_candidate_places) is unusual in the surviving Arabic lot literature and directly links Chapter IV's hyleg doctrine to Chapter V's lot doctrine.

exceptions: The Lot of Hyleg's formula is stated without a 'by night the reverse' clause, unlike almost every other lot in this chapter; this omission is preserved as stated rather than assumed to be an editorial gap.

rules.period: mid-10th century CE (composed for Sayf al-Dawla, Aleppo); Wurzburg TEI derived from the 2004 critical edition

scope.unit: a representative set of the ~50 house-topic lots, with named-author attributions

conditions.trigger: casting lots for wealth, marriage, death, and sultanate specifically

conclusion.arabic: البيت الثاني سهم المال يؤخذ بالنهار والليل من ربّ بيت المال إلى درجة ودقيقة بيت المال ويلقى من الطالع ... سهم تزويج النساء لهرمس يؤخذ بالنهار والليل من الزهرة إلى زحل ويلقى من الطالع ... سهم تزويج النساء لواليس يؤخذ بالنهار والليل من الشمس إلى القمر ويلقى من الطالع ... سهم الموت يؤخذ بالنهار والليل من القمر إلى درجة ودقيقة بيت الثامن ويلقى من درجة زحل ... سهم العمل والسلطان لواليس يؤخذ بالنهار والليل من الشمس إلى درجة وسط السماء ويلقى من الطالع
conclusion.engine_rendering: Second house, the Lot of Wealth: taken by day and night alike from the lord of the wealth-house to the degree and minute of the wealth-house, cast from the Ascendant [...]. The Lot of Women's Marriage according to Hermes: from Venus to Saturn, cast from the Ascendant. The Lot of Women's Marriage according to Valens: from the Sun to the Moon, cast from the Ascendant. The Lot of Death: from the Moon to the degree and minute of the eighth house, cast from Saturn's degree. The Lot of Work and Sultanate according to Valens: from the Sun to the Midheaven's degree, cast from the Ascendant.
conclusion.lot_of_wealth_2nd_house: by day and night alike, from the lord of the 2nd house's own place to the 2nd-house cusp's degree and minute; cast from the Ascendant
conclusion.lot_of_mens_marriage_7th: by day and night alike, from the Sun to Venus, cast from the Ascendant
conclusion.lot_of_womens_marriage_hermes_7th: attributed to Hermes by name: by day and night alike, from Venus to Saturn, cast from the Ascendant
conclusion.lot_of_womens_marriage_valens_7th: attributed to Valens (Walis) by name, as an alternative to Hermes's formula: by day and night alike, from the Sun to the Moon, cast from the Ascendant
conclusion.lot_of_death_8th: by day and night alike, from the Moon to the 8th house's own degree and minute, cast from Saturn's degree (not from the Ascendant - an explicit exception to the chapter's general casting point)
conclusion.lot_of_sultanate_valens_10th: attributed to Valens (Walis) by name: by day and night alike, from the Sun to the Midheaven's degree, cast from the Ascendant
conclusion.lot_of_friends_andarzaghar_variant_11th: the base formula is from the Moon to Mercury, cast from the Ascendant; al-Andarzaghar is cited by name for a variant night formula (reversed), and al-Qabisi notes 'it is fitting to use both lots together'
conclusion.lot_of_enemies_hermes_12th: attributed to Hermes by name: by day and night alike, from the lord of the 12th house to the 12th house's own degree, cast from the Ascendant; 'some of the ancients' (an unnamed alternative) instead give: from Saturn to Mars, cast from the Ascendant

exceptions: Only 8 of the roughly 50 lots the chapter lists for the 12 houses are reproduced individually here as representative examples; the full inventory is noted in islam.qabisi.ch5.additional_named_lots and the chapter's own closing disclosure rather than transcribed lot-by-lot.

scope.unit: additional non-house-bound lots, and the chapter's own closing inventory statement

conditions.trigger: lots for intellectual/military/informational topics, used often by astrologers per al-Qabisi's own note

conclusion.arabic: وهاهنا سهام أخر يستعملها أصحاب أحكام النجوم كثيرا ... فهذه جملة ما وقع إلينا من السهام وإنّما أتينا هذه السهام الأخيرة وإن كان القول فيها ضعيفا لئلّا نترك شيئا ممّا يجوز أن يكون مدخلا إلى صناعة أحكام النجوم إلّا أتينا به وبالله التوفيق
conclusion.engine_rendering: And here are other lots frequently used by astrologers [...]. This is the sum of what has come down to us of the lots. We have brought these last lots even though the doctrine concerning them is weak, so as not to leave out anything that might serve as an introduction to the art of astrology - and success is from God.
conclusion.additional_lots_named: the truth or falsehood of a report; intellect and profundity; wisdom; knowledge; war and battle; peace among armies; a lot 'for looking into the revolution of the year'
conclusion.chapter_inventory_statement: al-Qabisi closes the chapter by stating this is 'jumlat ma waqa'a ilayna min al-sihaam' (the sum of what has come down to us of the lots), and that he included even the weakest of them (the mundane commodity-price lots that follow, see islam.qabisi.ch5.commodity_price_lots_self_declared_weak) deliberately, so as not to omit anything that might serve as an introduction to the art

exceptions: This rule records the chapter's own closing self-assessment; it is not this pass's assessment of the material.

scope.unit: 'the two greatest lots' for the duration of a kingship/dynasty

conditions.trigger: estimating how long a ruling power will endure, from the ascendant of the founding conjunction and later year-revolutions

conclusion.arabic: عمل السهمين الأعظمين المستخرج بهما مدّة قيام الملك فالأوّل منهما أن تنظر في وقت قيام الملك إلى أين انتهت السنة من قران المثلّثة التي دلّت على الملّة
conclusion.engine_rendering: The working of the two greatest lots, by which the duration of a kingship is derived: the first of them is that you look, at the time the ruler takes power, to where the year has arrived from the triplicity-conjunction that signified the dynasty.
conclusion.method_summary: two lots are cast from two different oriental/occidental planet pairings (Saturn/Jupiter relative to the Sun) at the founding conjunction and at the revolution marking the ruler's accession, then combined; al-Qabisi calls this ''amal al-sahmayn al-a'zamayn' (the working of the two greatest lots)
conclusion.commodity_context: this section is presented alongside a separate lot for the general strength/weakness of a reign, and a note that a planet's rising/falling condition at the relevant revolution shows whether the reign will be prosperous or troubled

exceptions: This is explicitly mundane/dynastic doctrine; recorded for completeness only.

scope.unit: commodity/food price-divination lots, with al-Qabisi's own explicit caveat

conditions.trigger: world-year revolution lots used to divine whether specific goods will be expensive or cheap

conclusion.arabic: سهم الطعام من الشمس إلى المرّيخ سهم الماء من القمر إلى الزهرة سهم الشعير من القمر إلى المشتري ... سهم السموم من الجوزهر إلى زحل ويلقى جميع ذلك من طالع التحويل
conclusion.engine_rendering: The Lot of Food: from the Sun to Mars. The Lot of Water: from the Moon to Venus. The Lot of Barley: from the Moon to Jupiter [... and so through the remaining named goods] ... The Lot of Poisons: from the node to Saturn. All of these are cast from the revolution's Ascendant.
conclusion.method_summary: for each named good, a lot is cast from the year-revolution's Ascendant; its placement in a domicile/exaltation/bound/triplicity ruled by a planet in good or poor condition (direct/retrograde, combust, angular, aspected by benefics or malefics) signals whether that good will be cheap or dear
conclusion.named_goods: food in general, water, barley, chickpeas, lentils, broad beans, mash-beans, dates, honey, rice, olives, grapes, cotton, sesame, melon, and four taste-categories (sour, sweet, pungent, bitter foods), plus three categories of laxative medicine (sweet, sour, salty) and poisons (cast from the node to Saturn)
conclusion.self_declared_caveat: al-Qabisi explicitly flags this entire set as weak doctrine in his own closing statement (see islam.qabisi.ch5.additional_named_lots_and_inventory): 'we have brought these last lots even though the doctrine concerning them is weak.' This is the source's OWN epistemic caveat, not one invented for this pass.

exceptions: This is the single most marginal material in the chapter by al-Qabisi's own explicit admission; included for completeness of the source record, never for output.
